newsitem.title: INDIA: India BSE expansion seen drawing small investors.
newsitem.headline: India BSE expansion seen drawing small investors.

text.p: Plans by the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) to expand to other Indian cities will give small investors across the country access to improved liquidity and better prices, the bourse chief said on Wednesday.
BSE president Madan Gopal Damani said the BSE had about 7,000 shares listed but only one-third were traded every day.
"The 4,500 scrips which have become illiquid will become liquid," he told Reuters. "If investors are able to buy and sell at will, then naturally they will be tempted to come again."

Investors have stayed away from Indian bourses for the last two years after they were saddled with worthless paper bought at huge premium during a short-lived boom soon after India unshackled its socialist economy in 1991.
"Particularly in the interest of investors, BSE will definitely become a gainer....business will increase," Damani said.
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Tuesday it had approved BSE's proposal to set up its trading screens across India subject to certain conditions.

Damani said the BSE has already signed an agreement with the Ahmedabad exchange in western Gujarat state and hopes to reach similar arrangements with five more regional stock exchanges by November to open BSE's branches in their respective cities.
The BSE chief said SEBI's move to reduce the minimum application lot for primary issues to 200 shares from 500 shares will make stock investments accessible to small investors.
The president said the BSE expects to start a depository by the first quarter of 1997, a move widely expected to eliminate problems of huge share transfers now manually carried out by brokers.
The exchange's plan to establish a trade guarantee scheme, to provide guarantees of all transactions between its members, will be finalised in November.
"We are committed to doing it," Damani said.
